identity.title: Charcot triad at the bedside (fever + RUQ pain/tenderness + jaundice)

technique.how: Document all three elements at the same encounter: fever (or rigors), right-upper-quadrant pain or tenderness on palpation, and jaundice (scleral icterus in good light, confirmed by bilirubin when available). The triad is positive only when all three are present.
technique.prerequisites: Recorded temperature; inspection of sclerae; RUQ palpation.

interpretation.positive_finding: The full triad is highly specific (0.96-0.99) for acute cholangitis and should trigger blood cultures, antibiotics and early biliary imaging with drainage planning. It does not separate cholangitis from acute cholecystitis with jaundice (false-positive rate 11.9% in acute cholecystitis in the TG13 cohort).
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of the full triad does not exclude cholangitis: sensitivity is only 0.26-0.46, so most cholangitis patients lack it. Use Tokyo Guidelines criteria (systemic inflammation + cholestasis + biliary imaging) rather than the triad to rule out.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sensitivity is very low; elderly, immunosuppressed and post-ERCP patients may present with confusion or hypotension without pain. Jaundice may be absent early or with partial obstruction.
interpretation.changes_what: Triad present: treat as cholangitis (cultures, antibiotics, urgent biliary imaging/drainage). Triad absent: still apply TG18 criteria; never use absence to rule out.

estimates.target_condition: Acute cholangitis (TG13 gold standard: purulent bile, or clinical remission after biliary drainage, or remission with antibiotics alone with biliary tree the only infection site); Charcot triad = fever + jaundice + RUQ pain
estimates.population: 1,432 retrospectively analysed biliary disease cases with suspected acute cholangitis, multiple tertiary centres in Japan (TG13 derivation cohort)
estimates.reference_standard: Purulent bile at drainage, or remission after biliary drainage, or remission with antibiotics alone (biliary tree sole infection site)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.264/(1-0.956) = 6.0; LR- = (1-0.264)/0.956 = 0.77; from abstract sensitivity 26.4% and specificity 95.6% (no CIs reported in abstract)
estimates.quote: The sensitivity of Charcot's triad was only 26.4 % but the specificity was 95.6 %.

estimates.target_condition: Acute cholangitis ('real-world cholangitis', clinical reference standard) in patients with suspected biliary obstruction undergoing ERCP; Charcot triad present
estimates.population: 794 patients with suspected biliary obstruction who underwent ERCP, nationwide prospective Dutch cohort (127 with cholangitis)
estimates.reference_standard: Real-world cholangitis diagnosis by treating clinicians (clinical reference standard) in patients undergoing ERCP
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.46/(1-0.99) = 46; LR- = (1-0.46)/0.99 = 0.55; from abstract sensitivity 46% and specificity 99%. Prevalence 127/794 = 0.16 from abstract.
estimates.quote: The sensitivity for DPSG and Charcot was 42% (95% CI 33-51) and 46% (95% CI 38-56), specificity was 99.7% (95% CI 99-100) and 99% (95% CI 98-100), respectively.

sources.citation: Kiriyama S, Takada T, Strasberg SM et al. New diagnostic criteria and severity assessment of acute cholangitis in revised Tokyo Guidelines. Journal of hepato-biliary-pancreatic sciences. 2013.

Sperna Weiland CJ, Busch CBE, Bhalla A et al. Performance of diagnostic tools for acute cholangitis in patients with suspected biliary obstruction. Journal of hepato-biliary-pancreatic sciences. 2022.
Kiriyama S, Kozaka K, Takada T et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018: diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholangitis (with videos). Journal of hepato-biliary-pancreatic sciences. 2018.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of the triad to defer work-up in a septic, confused or hypotensive patient with biliary risk factors (stones, stents, prior ERCP, malignancy).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Triad plus hypotension or altered mentation (Reynolds pentad) indicates severe (Grade III) cholangitis: urgent biliary decompression and sepsis management.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data for the triad located; each component (fever, RUQ tenderness, jaundice) is subject to the usual examiner variability of those signs (unverified recall).

extraction_notes: Two cohorts, deliberately kept separate. (1) Kiriyama 2013 (TG13 derivation, PMID 22825491): retrospective 1,432 suspected-cholangitis cases; Charcot triad sensitivity 26.4%, specificity 95.6%; abstract also states 'the false positive rate in cases of acute cholecystitis was 11.9 %' (Abstract, Results). Prevalence not in abstract; full text not on PMC. LRs computed from sens/spec. (2) Sperna Weiland 2022 (PMID 34932265): prospective, 794 ERCP patients, '127 (16%) of 794 patients were diagnosed with real-world cholangitis' and '66 (8%) ... were defined as having cholangitis' by Charcot (Abstract, Results); sensitivity 46% (38-56), specificity 99% (98-100). Higher sensitivity than TG13 cohort reflects a pre-selected ERCP population and a clinical reference standard. TG18 (Kiriyama 2018, PMID 29032610) cited as the guideline that replaced the triad with TG13/18 criteria; its abstract carries no triad numbers. Spectrum: neither cohort is an undifferentiated ED abdominal-pain population, so LR+ of 46 should be read as an upper bound.
